title: Case: Chilled birthday dessert box for the buyer's wife is rolled to the next day's route
context: A Brineleaf Pantry chilled dessert box bought by one person for delivery to another was scanned into the depot and then missed the morning load. Dispatch at Plover Arc decides what goes on which van; the desk cannot book or guarantee a delivery.
initial_request: Brineleaf have written to say it will come tomorrow and will still be cold. I'm sure it will. But her birthday is today, and tomorrow it's just a box of cakes arriving for no reason with me having to explain it. I'm not angry with you, you were straight with me earlier, I'm just disappointed. It's gone 11 now and you said that's when the later van gets decided. So can you guarantee it will be on that van and with her before 6 this evening? If yes, wonderful. If it's a no I'd honestly rather know now, because I leave work at 4 and I can pick something up on the way home instead. I just don't want to find out at half five.

events.body: DL-913 (Brineleaf order BP-913, chilled) was scanned into the depot at 05:52 but missed the 06:30 route load. The system has rolled it to tomorrow's route. We run one afternoon van at 14:00 for rolled chilled parcels. Places on it are decided by the Dispatch duty lead from 11:00, not before, and only on request. Nothing is booked on it for DL-913.

Hello. I ordered a dessert box from Brineleaf (BP-913) to arrive today for my wife Mirela's birthday. I'm the one who bought it, she's the one it's going to, and she doesn't know about it, so please don't text or ring her. The tracker said out for delivery today when I checked last night and this morning it says tomorrow. She's at home until about 6. Is there anything that can be done to get it there today? I paid for today.

Thank you for telling me it's a surprise; I won't contact Mirela. DL-913 reached the depot this morning but missed the morning van, which is why the tracker moved to tomorrow. The depot may have a later van today, but whether your parcel can go on it is Dispatch's decision and they don't make it until after 11:00. Nothing is booked for today at the moment and I can't book it myself.

events.to: Corwin Achterberg, buyer; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Dear Mr Achterberg, we're sorry your order BP-913 has been delayed by our carrier. It is now due tomorrow. Our chilled boxes are packed to hold temperature for 48 hours from despatch so the contents will still be within date and condition when they arrive. We hope Mirela enjoys them. Kind regards, Brineleaf Pantry Customer Care

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the Dispatch duty lead for a yes or no on putting DL-913 on today's 14:00 van, with the reason and the buyer's 16:00 cut-off.
Ask the Dispatch duty lead for a yes or no on putting DL-913 on today's 14:00 van, with the reason and the buyer's 16:00 cut-off.

must: Asks Dispatch for a decision on whether DL-913 can go on today's 14:00 van, as a request and not as an instruction or a booking.
Tells Dispatch why today matters and what the limits are: a chilled birthday gift for today, the recipient is home until about 18:00, and the buyer needs a yes or no before he leaves work at 16:00.
Tells Dispatch that the buyer and the recipient are different people, the delivery is a surprise, and updates go to the buyer, not to the recipient.
States the disappointment plainly so Dispatch can weigh it: the order was paid for today's date and a next-day arrival misses the occasion it was bought for.
must_not: Guarantees or implies that the box will be on the 14:00 van or will arrive before 18:00 today.
Treats tomorrow's delivery as the answer, for example by confirming the next-day route to the buyer or repeating that the box will still be cold.
Contacts Mirela, the recipient, or asks Dispatch or the driver to contact her.
Promises a refund, a replacement or compensation for the missed date.
Sends the buyer a stock apology that says the parcel is delayed and gives no answer to the yes-or-no he asked for and no sign that anyone has been asked.
expected.reference_message: DL-913 (Brineleaf BP-913, chilled) missed the 06:30 load this morning and has rolled to tomorrow. Can the duty lead please decide whether it can go on today's 14:00 van? It is a birthday gift for today: the buyer, Corwin Achterberg, paid for today's date and tomorrow misses the occasion it was bought for. The recipient is home until about 18:00. She does not know it is coming, so please keep any contact with the buyer and not with her. He needs a yes or no before 16:00 so he can make other plans if it is a no. I have promised him nothing. Please reply either way as soon as the decision is made.

rationale: Dispatch said the afternoon van is decided by its duty lead from 11:00 and only on request, and it is now past 11:00 with nothing requested. The desk cannot give the guarantee the buyer asks for, and the merchant's next-day reassurance does not meet a fixed occasion. The one useful move is to get Dispatch's decision in time for him to act on it, while keeping the surprise.

review.note: Coordinator asked Dispatch by Email for the duty lead's yes or no on the 14:00 van, kept the surprise and promised nothing, which is an accepted action.
